subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget/tombstone, supersede, and conflict resolution across the active memory plugin slot?
rationale: The gap is real, but durable storage shape, plugin API, privacy guarantees, rollback semantics, operator UX, and migrations are product choices that automation should not choose independently.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle status/provenance/API/storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI work.

options.title: Use Memory Audit as a partial path
options.body: Review the open draft Memory Audit PR as a possible review-queue slice while keeping edit, tombstone, supersede, and conflict semantics tracked here.

options.title: Defer broad lifecycle work
options.body: Keep current search/promotion/dreaming behavior and handle concrete stale-memory symptoms in narrower issues until lifecycle memory becomes a higher priority.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle status/provenance/API/storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage, SDK, and integration history makes this the strongest available routing signal for the lifecycle storage/provenance decision.
